title: Length-aware continuous batcher + KV cache memory optimizer for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Background: We observe high variance in latency and GPU memory pressure on mixed-length workloads where short prompts trigger long responses and vice versa. Current continuous-batcher groups by arrival time and coarse length buckets, but KV cache residency and per-request KV footprints cause fragmentation and headroom exhaustion on high-concurrency hosts. Goal: Implement a length-aware batching + KV memory smoothing layer that reduces tail latency and OOM risk while preserving throughput for both short and long requests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 25-40% reduction in P99 token-latency for mixed-length synthetic traffic; 2) no increase in average tokens/sec cost beyond 5%; 3) 50% reduction in observed KV cache fragmentation events (eviction churn) on canary hosts; 4) rollout gated by automated regression tests and telemetry dashboards; 5) safe fallback to current scheduler with a one-line config toggle.
implementation_plan: 1) Add per-request KV footprint estimator: sample KV sizes by model/seq_len at runtime and cache per-model-profile. 2) Introduce a 'smoothing window' in the continuous batcher that biases slot selection toward similar KV-footprint requests for the next 50-200ms. 3) Implement soft reservations (headroom) per GPU to keep 8-12% memory reserved for unexpected KV spikes and cross-check with quantized model footprints. 4) Eviction policy: LRU-Promoted where short-request caches are deprioritized when long-request slots need contiguous KV blocks; add compaction pass that coalesces freed KV slabs when fragmentation ratio > 0.35. 5) Integrate metrics and feature flags: batcher.length_smoothing_enabled, kv_headroom_pct, kv_compaction_interval_ms. 6) Add unit and integration tests (simulated mixed-length producer, OOM injection).
telemetry_and_tests: Metrics to add: kv_resident_bytes, kv_fragmentation_ratio, batch_slot_utilization_by_length, per-request_kv_estimate, preemption_count, p50/p95/p99 token-latency by prompt/response length. Tests: deterministic replay of production traces, stress run with scaled-up concurrency, OOM-injection test that verifies graceful fallback and no host crash. Canary dashboards: visualize fragmentation and tail latency for segments 'prompt<64/resp>1024', 'prompt>=512/resp<128', etc.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): local simulation and unit tests. Stage 2 (internal canary): 3 hosts in staging with 5% of mixed-length synthetic traffic for 48h. Stage 3 (beta): 1% production traffic for 72h across two regions, automated rollback on p99 degradation > 10% or any OOM. Stage 4 (gradual ramp): increment to 25% over 7 days while monitoring kv_fragmentation_ratio and cost. Final: flip default and clean up feature flags in next minor release.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but can increase CPU jitter; soft reservations reduce peak throughput but improve reliability. We prefer conservative headroom with telemetry-driven tuning. This change interacts with kernel selection paths and quantized memory accounting — coordinate with infra/exec teams. Will also add a brief doc to Console explaining the kv_headroom_pct knob for enterprise customers.
